1_toolaccess_limitations:
- Reddit content was entirely inaccessible. Zero Reddit thread URLs were returned by the search engine across 30+ query formulations, and direct Reddit URL fetches were blocked by the web_fetch tool's provenance requirement. This is the largest gap in source-venue coverage. The single Reddit-attributed quote (F-P13) was recovered from a secondary blog source and carries reduced provenance confidence.
- YouTube video transcripts were inaccessible due to tool limitations with video/audio content.
- Etsy's fees policy page (etsy.com/legal/fees) returned 403 Forbidden on direct fetch; fee content was recovered from the Sell page FAQ (F-04) and search index snippets.
2_sourcetype_taxonomy_application:
- Trustpilot (F-X06) was assigned source_type `unknown` per shard instruction: "review_aggregator" is not in the 18-value closed enum. Note added per shard rule.
- G2 and Capterra do not index Etsy as a product (F-X02, F-X05), so no source_type assignment was needed.
- All Etsy blog/news pages (etsy.com/news/*) were assigned `blog`. Etsy's seller policy page was assigned `policy_page`. Etsy's About and Sell pages were assigned `platform_doc`.
3_verification_methodology:
- Part 1 findings were marked `direct_verified` only when the full page was successfully fetched by a subagent AND the verbatim text was confirmed present on the page. Four sources (Big Cartel, DropInBlog, GoDaddy, Thunderbit) underwent a secondary verification fetch to confirm search-snippet-captured passages appeared on the live page.
- Part 2 findings were marked `blocked_url_index_verified` when the page was not fully fetched but verbatim text was recovered from search engine snippets or partial page loads.
4_scope_boundary_decisions:
- Trustpilot Temu comparison (F-X06): degraded to Part 4 as borderline D2/D5. The competitive reference is secondary to complaint content.
- Big Cartel fee-breakdown passage ("You'll pay $0.20 to list an item, plus a 6.5% transaction fee, plus 3% + $0.25 for payment processing. If you're roped into their offsite ads program, wave goodbye to up to 15% more.") was verified on the page but not reported as a separate finding due to substantive overlap with F-04 (Etsy's own fee description), F-07 (Mercury fee-stacking), and F-09 (Lovable quantified fees). The fee dimension is well-covered by existing findings.
- GoDaddy "unlike eBay, Etsy isn't built for dropshipping" passage and Shopify Blog's Etsy product-policy passage were verified but not reported as separate findings; the product-policy positioning angle overlaps with F-P02 (seller policy) and is closer to D1 (feature/policy description) than D5 (competitive positioning).
5_affiliate_and_affiliation_disclosures_:
- Shopify Blog (F-11, F-P03, F-P12): published by Shopify, a direct competitor to Etsy. Noted in each finding.
- Big Cartel Blog (F-12): published by Big Cartel, a direct competitor. Noted.
- Sellfy Blog (F-P09): published by Sellfy, a competitor to both Etsy and Gumroad. Noted.
- SellerLogic (F-P06): sells Amazon seller tools (Amazon-ecosystem affiliation). Noted.
- Nav.com (F-14): general advertiser disclaimer, not specific to Etsy or Amazon. Noted.
- GoDaddy (F-13): promotes its own e-commerce product via CTAs. Noted.
- Thunderbit (F-15): promotes its own scraper tool. Noted.
- Mercury (F-06, F-07, F-08): no e-commerce platform affiliation detected.
- Lovable (F-09, F-10): no Etsy/Shopify affiliation; promotes its own AI product.
- No source disclosed paid affiliation with Etsy specifically.
6_output_shape_assessment:
- Part 1: 15 clean findings (guidance: 8–15). At upper bound; all genuinely direct_verified.
- Part 2: 13 provisional findings (guidance: 10–15). Within range.
- Part 4: 7 entries (guidance: 5–10). Within range.
- No findings were invented to meet quotas. No verification bars were lowered.
